links.reason: Innaa 33 line 1 'கள்ளுண்பான் கூறுங் கருமப் பொருளின்னா' and Muthumozhikkanchi 'கள்ளுண் போன்சோர்வு இன்மை பொய்' share only the drinker; the second says he is not free of lapses, which is not a cause the first names. A shared topic, not a development.

Kural 379 asks why one who takes good as good grieves at ill; 1167 line 3-4 'புலம்பலு மகிழ்வு ... இன்றி ... ஊழ்வினை யென்று விட்டான்' removes joy as well as grief, which is a real narrowing of the couplet. The note describes both ends accurately.

848 'ஆம்பொருள்க ளாகுமது ... போம்பொருள்கள் போகும்' agrees with Kural 376 on what is destined staying or going, but the verse itself says nothing of a dispossessed heir or an offer of arms; that is the marker's reconstruction (event None). Teaches and gains both rest on context outside the verse.

The verse (line 3-4 'சித்தியிற் படர் சிந்தையினாரையும் இத்திசைப் படர்') draws release-seekers back by the women's breasts; the Siddhar reproaches his own heart for lust. These are not incompatible claims, both treat women's pull as a lapse from the goal, so tension is the wrong type. The gains claim that being drawn back is 'ruin' for the epic is not in the verse, which is praise.

1276 line 2 'குறைவளி பித்தொடு ஐயில் பிண்டித்து' reports one healer's diagnosis among rivals (என்பார்), and the last line says all spells failed; it does not show the humoral theory failing as a doctrine or sound medicine misapplied. The Kural speaks of food and work in excess or want, which a snakebite does not test; the 'limit' is invented. Verse flagged uncertain.

257 is Madanan's retort 'தோளினால் வலியர்... வாளினால் பேசல்', but he never denies the claim about Fortune; scorning talk is not an incompatible claim, so tension fits poorly. That the warning 'will be made good' by the story is not in either verse.

183 prefers death to backbiting without any afterlife claim, and the Kural never assumes death ends all; 1937 only lists tongue-tearing for slanderers 'குறிப்பல சொல்லிய நாவை'. The 'ethical comparison before any hell' in the epic verse is absent. Illustration of punishment, not a development.

605 is a Jain proclamation for the whole city to practise penance (தவம், பவம் நீங்க); 2389 is a wedding proclamation to dress in finery. Different occasions, different advice; no incompatible claim, only the shared word of the drum. The 'unreconciled ideals' lesson is the grader's theme, not the Tamil's.

Soolamani 1 line 1-4 says he conquered karma and those who bowed at his feet were freed, but the marker's own nuance admits the verse does not say whether bowing or the god's example frees them; so it names no ground for the feet's power. Kural 10 'இறைவன் அடிசேரா தார்' and 'வினை நீங்கி நின்றார்' agree in theme; 'qualifies' and the stated gains are read in.

219 only says she saw three dreams (3 'கனவு மூன்று') and trembled; the dream of the falling tree and the sprout is in 223, not in the unit. Sil 20 lines 2 'குடையொடு கோல்வீழ' is a real parallel omen of the king's fall, but the teaches contrast rests on text outside the linked unit.

Innaa 4 line 4 'பெருவலியார்க் கின்னா செயல்' and Pazhamozhi 302 'வலியாரைக் கண்டக்கால் வாய்வாளாராகி' do agree on caution before the strong. But the proverb's 'மேன்மை' may be ironic and the verse is flagged uncertain; the pair adds only a cause/remedy framing.

237 line 4 'எண்ணாயிரம்' beats 227 'மூவாயிரங்கை', but 237 does not name Mananigai nor say whose side she plays, and 227 does not say Ariyai silenced Dattai's side as a rival score. The 'ladder' is story sequence; the verses stand in order.

290 'தின்றனைமு னென்றே ... செம்புகள் திணிப்ப' makes the penalty mirror the meal, a real point beyond Kural 255 'அளறு அண்ணாத்தல் செய்யாது'. But the Kural's image is hell's mouth not opening (no release), not hell feeding the eater, so 'develops' flips the image; this is mostly the same warning against flesh-eating.

463 'பூமியும் புணர்க' and 2417 'வையம் நின்னடி நிழலின் வைக நேமியஞ் செல்வனாகி' are both women's blessings of earthly rule, and the later is the fuller; but the words differ, 2417 is spoken to a bridegroom at a ghee-anointing, and the 'standing has risen' lesson is plot knowledge, not what the pair shows.

Naladiyar 23 turns wedding drums to funeral drums and sends the worthy to the way of escape; 1394 line 1-2 'இளமையின் மூப்பும் ... புணர்ச்சிப் போழ்திற் கிளைநரிற் பிரிவு' is a list of reversals used to console. Shared impermanence theme with different uses; the verse's uses it to forbid grief, not to seek release, so it is not a development of the quatrain.

351 line 3 'வளை கை உடைத்து' and Pur 253 line 5 'வளைஇல், வறுங்கை' share the bare arm; the Sangam poem makes it a widow's dread. But 351 gives a farewell to jewels in an ascetic initiation and does not itself state widowhood; the widow reading is the marker's. Purananuru poem flagged uncertain.

1790 'கம்பெறி களிநல் யானைக் கடற்படை' only seats the kings for the choosing; Naladiyar 21 says elephant-borne kings are dead. The verse says nothing of impermanence or a failed show of force, so the 'measure' it gains is brought in from outside; shared elephants and kings only.

1810 'உக்கிரமெய்க் குலத்தரசன்' praises by line and Naladiyar 195 'தவம்கல்வி யாள்வினை என்றிவற்றான் ஆகும் குலம்' denies birth rank; a real contrast. But the herald announces candidates and does not claim lineage makes worth, so qualifies is thin; the pair mainly shows the convention.

316 line 3 'கொண்டு போம் ஒருவன் இன்னே' foretells a man who will take the child away at once; 320 'வாளொடு கனை இருள் வந்து தோன்றினான்' shows Kantukkatan arriving at night. The later unit fulfils the earlier, and the note names it accurately.

1909 line 2 'பல்லியும் பட்ட' and Akananuru 289 line 15 'பகுவாய்ப் பல்லி படுதொறும்' share the lizard omen, but it is a general omen, not distinctively akam. The claim that the epic reads as near-erotic longing, and that the akam image gains a non-erotic use, is read in. Line 3 'சோந்து' looks corrupt.

2846 gives release by knowledge, faith and conduct burning karma by effort; 2849 line 3 'வல்லையே பணிமின் அடிகள்' calls for worship to clear sin, which the sermon verse does not make a first step. The note's 'doctrine becomes a practice' is invented; the speaker of 2849 is also uncertain.

196 'சயந்தியி னின்றும் போந்து' departs Jayanti for a Kausambi grove and 120 'சயந்தி புக்குப்' enters Jayanti: a story-order sequence. 196 only reaches a grove outside Kausambi so nothing is 'completed'.

636 line 4 'வீட்டுலகங் காணார்' and Kural 1103 'தாமரைக் கண்ணான் உலகு' both weigh a beloved's beauty against a higher world. But the epic is narrator's hyperbole, not an inherited lover's voice, and the 'peril to the soul' answer is the marker's, not the verse's.

Naladiyar 42 line 1-4 treats the body as a covered bag of openings to be looked at without desire; Kural 80 'என்புதோல் போர்த்த உடம்பு' is for the loveless. The Naladiyar does not mention love or an exception, so 'allows no such exception' is an inference; the two address different questions.

879 line 4 'வெல்வது சூதென' calls a powder contest a wager, with no stake, vow or shame stated; the gains cites a 'கண்ணற்றார்' not in the verse. Kural 931 'வேண்டற்க வென்றிடினும் சூதினை' is about dice and the link rests on the word சூது.

583 'வரிந்த கச்சைய னொருவன்' is unnamed; identifying him with Turumakanthan of 116 'துரும காந்தனைக் காவல் வைத்துமே' is the marker's guess (nuance says 'likely'), so 'the plan worked' is not in the Tamil. Verse flagged uncertain.

Naga 58 shows a prince taming a literal horse for show; Tirumanthiram 1679 'ஒடுங் குதிரைக் குசைதிண்ணம் பற்றுமின்' uses the horse for the mind. A real horse and a figurative one share a word, not an image used in the same way.

388 'அருந் தவன் முந்து கூற' refers back to a foretelling and 1130 'புண்ணியற் பெறுதி ரென்ன' gives the sage's word; that link is real. But 'a mother in despair' and 'capture and rescue' are not in 1130, which says only that more was told the merchant privately.

1318 'மலையெடுத்திடுகோ ... நிகரெனக் குளரே' is a boast and Naladiyar 346 'சக்கரச் செல்வம் பெறினும் ... மிகுதிச்சொல்' says the excellent do not boast; it illustrates the rule. The fall 'in the next verses' is not in the unit, so teaches and gains over-read it.

1451 'ஆயிரம் பணத்த தாய ... நாக' shoots a naga weapon and 1452 'உவணப் புள்ளி னுருவினோர் தெய்வ வம்பு' answers with a Garuda arrow that tears it with its beak. The later verse answers the earlier by the natural enemy, as the note says.

960 'கதழக் கூப்பினார்' has two princes bow to a king at a wedding meeting; Kural 680 says small rulers bow to the great out of fear. Nothing in 960 says they are equals, allies or free; the pair shares only a bow.

146 line 3 'உள்ளு காமம் உள் சுட' only states the king's desire in a pavilion description; the loss of kingdom and life is not in the verse and it is not a seductive scene. Kural 901 'மனைவிழைவார் மாண்பயன் எய்தார்' is a general warning, so 'develops' stretches the pair.

215 line 2 'முனம் ஆகிய பான்மை முளைத்து' blames former deeds and the king's heart; 1670 line 2 'இஃதூழ் வினையா' gives destiny for Civakan's love, but who speaks is uncertain and no 'pause of scruple' appears. The pairing is a shared explanation, not a development.

Yasodhara 63 line 2 'இன்னபல் பிறவி தோறும் இடும்பைகள் தொடர்ந்த' ties old harm to living bodies to suffering across births; Naladiyar 101 'பழவினையும் ... கிழவனை நாடிக் கொளற்கு' says an old deed seeks its doer. They are the same karma claim, with the epic adding the kind of deed.

3072 line 4 'இன்னுயிர் ஓம்பினான்' could mean guarding creatures or his own life and line 1-2 are hard; Kural 261 'உற்றநோய் நோன்றல் உயிர்க்குறுகண் செய்யாமை' fits only on the first reading. An illustration of tapas, conditional on that reading.
links.text_issue: lines 1-2 hard to parse; இன்னுயிர் ஓம்பினான் ambiguous

links.reason: 114 line 3-4 'சாலமந் திரமங் காதில் ... தேவா யிற்றே' and 943 line 3-4 'செல்கதி மந்திர நீயுடம் பட்டு நினைமதி' both tell of a dying animal and a mantra. The difference of dog consenting versus elephant simply hearing is a difference in what each verse chooses to say, not shown doctrine; 'at once' is not stated.

18 line 3-4 'சித்தம் குழையற்க எனத் தீர்த்து' and 1285 'புலம்புகொண் டழேற்க' are a comfort word and a promise; the later gives no diagnosis, and healers' rivalry is in other verses. The teaches rests on the next three verses, outside the unit.

943 promises the dog 'சேயுடம் பெய்துவை' a god's body of sun-like light if it thinks on the mantra; 1172 has the god say the man relieved him in the dog's birth and gave him this body ('எனக்கருளி'). The later verse fulfils and remembers the earlier, as the note states.

Both lines use 'யாங்கு வல்லுநள்கொல் தானே' with refused milk, a shared formula, not a development. The note says both are foster mothers, but Akananuru 105's speaker is the mother (the foster mothers offer the milk), and 'tenderness' versus 'fear' is not in the verses.

173 gives Padumai in marriage after the war of 172, and the marker reads the marriage as its reward, but neither verse says it was payment; 172 only has the king return with tribute. It is the story's next step.

406 'இருவரு ளிளையவ னீண்டந் நம்பியே' names the younger son as the hero; 78 'இளய நம்பியே' gives the younger prince's marks. Same person, not a shared image, and 406 does not mention the marks; 'two proofs' is the marker's reading.

1154 'தோழனை நினைப்ப லென்றான்' has Civakan think of a friend; the dog and god appear only in other verses. The teaches reverses the debt: Kural 107 has the helped man remember, while here the helper calls on the debtor, and only one rebirth is involved, not seven.
links.text_issue: 1154 does not name the dog; relies on 943-948

links.reason: 1745 'பெயரிட்டுக் ... இன்பக் கடலாழ்ந்தான்' gives a naming and joy, with no father's praise or son called worthy; the marker flags the verse's sense uncertain. Kural 69 'சான்றோன் எனக்கேட்ட தாய்' rests on being praised as worthy, which the verse lacks.
